The similarity in the yield stresses and the activation volumes of the binary and Nb containing alloys leads us to believe that Nb substitutes into the Ti lattice sites and that the related strength increase is simply a consequence of the reduced aluminium content.
Thus, the high flow stress of TiAl alloys containing a large addition of Nb can be rationalized in terms of a Hall–Petch mechanism.
Appreciable improvements in high temperature strength and creep resistance have also been achieved by carbon additions.
